safetyNote: True morels must be identified with certainty and cooked thoroughly before eating. Raw or inadequately cooked morels have caused serious illness; even correctly identified morels can cause gastrointestinal or neurological symptoms. Seek medical advice promptly if symptoms follow a morel meal.

sections.title: Yellow morel
sections.text: Morchella esculenta is a spring morel with an oval to rounded cap. Its outer surface has deep, irregular, clearly bounded honeycomb pits separated by connected ridges; colour ranges from pale cream or yellow-ochre to honey brown. The lower cap margin is joined to the stem rather than hanging free. No gills or tubes occur under the cap: the fertile surface lines the pits.

sections.title: One continuous cavity
sections.text: A lengthwise cut through the entire fruit body reveals an open cavity continuing from the cap into the stem. The pale cream to whitish stem is hollow, often slightly ridged or granular, and may widen and wrinkle towards its base. There is no ring or volva. The hollow interior and fused cap margin are useful features, but neither one alone proves safe identification.

sections.title: Habitat and lookalikes
sections.text: In Europe, yellow morels appear mainly in spring, often from March to May depending on local conditions. They can occur at woodland edges, in damp broadleaf woods and in disturbed places such as paths or gardens. Gyromitra species have more lobed or brainlike caps and can be highly poisonous; some hollow or irregularly chambered lookalikes exist, so a single cut is not a universal exclusion test. The name 'yellow morel' is also applied to related Morchella species in different regions.

sections.title: Food safety
sections.text: Never eat morels raw or lightly cooked; cook identified specimens thoroughly. A US outbreak linked to a different true morel, M. sextelata, found a stronger association with illness when morels were served raw than when they were heated, but cooking does not establish a guarantee of safety. French poison-centre studies have also documented digestive and neurological illness after morel consumption, sometimes linked to large portions. Avoid excessive quantities and consult a qualified mycologist if identification is uncertain.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The white-background plate shows a whole yellow morel, a clean longitudinal section, a second whole view and a close-up of the cap's honeycomb pits. The section emphasises the uninterrupted hollow space and the cap margin fused to the stem.
